acceptance_criteria: The new whole-file module `ngv2/fp_filter.py` exists and exposes `FPPattern`, `load_fp_patterns`, `matches`, and `filter_findings` at module scope.
The module uses only the standard library (e.g. fnmatch, dataclasses) and has no third-party imports.
The module performs no network or file I/O operations.
All findings matching any of the loaded patterns are dropped by `filter_findings`, while other findings are preserved.
Verification command `python -m pytest tests/test_fp_filter.py -q` passes without errors in `/home/xnihil0zer0/NobleGreedv2`.

spec.objective: Implement a pure, deterministic, stdlib-only false-positive filtering module at `ngv2/fp_filter.py` to drop by-design or protocol-mandated false positives.
functional_requirements: Expose the `FPPattern` dataclass or class representing a criteria pattern for a false positive.
Expose the `load_fp_patterns` function that loads raw patterns and converts them into `FPPattern` objects.
Expose the `matches` function that checks if a finding matches a specific `FPPattern` or set of patterns.
Expose the `filter_findings` function that filters out matched false positive findings from a list of findings.
Module is pure, deterministic, stdlib-only, and performs no file/network I/O.
edge_cases: CWE matches exactly: finding['cwe'] must match pattern.cwe.
File matches via fnmatch: finding['file'] must match pattern.file_pattern using fnmatch pattern matching.
Code signature matches via substring check: pattern.code_signature must be a substring of finding['code'].
Empty collections: filter_findings returns all findings if patterns is empty, or empty if findings is empty, without raising errors.
non_goals: No file or network I/O — load_fp_patterns must not read real files or network resources (patterns are sourced from in-memory dictionary payload).
Do NOT author or modify any test/oracle (tests/test_fp_filter.py is already committed).
No dependency on the semgrep_adapter or confidence siblings, and no dependency on sibling sub-epics.
No cross-module wiring or integration glue.

# COMMITTED ORACLE CONTRACT (authoritative; you cannot read these files at synthesis time so they are reproduced verbatim -- your code MUST make them pass):

## tests/test_fp_filter.py
```python
"""RED oracle for ngv2.fp_filter — drop by-design / protocol-mandated false
positives by matching fp_patterns. Pure stdlib (fnmatch); operates on dicts."""
from dataclasses import is_dataclass

from ngv2.fp_filter import FPPattern, load_fp_patterns, matches, filter_findings


DATA = {
    'patterns': [
        {'id': 'fp_001', 'cwe': 'CWE-346', 'code_signature': 'postMessage(', 'file_pattern': '*sep24*',
         'reason': 'protocol_mandated'},
        {'id': 'fp_006', 'cwe': 'CWE-95', 'code_signature': 'ast.literal_eval', 'file_pattern': '*',
         'reason': 'safe_api'},
    ]
}


def test_fppattern_is_dataclass():
    assert is_dataclass(FPPattern)


def test_load_fp_patterns_fields():
    pats = load_fp_patterns(DATA)
    assert [p.id for p in pats] == ['fp_001', 'fp_006']
    assert pats[0].cwe == 'CWE-346'
    assert pats[0].reason == 'protocol_mandated'
    assert pats[0].file_pattern == '*sep24*'


def test_matches_requires_cwe_file_and_signature():
    pats = load_fp_patterns(DATA)
    fp1 = pats[0]
    hit = {'cwe': 'CWE-346', 'file': 'src/sep24_handler.js', 'code': 'window.postMessage(x, "*")'}
    assert matches(fp1, hit) is True
    # wrong cwe -> no match
    assert matches(fp1, {**hit, 'cwe': 'CWE-89'}) is False
    # wrong file -> no match
    assert matches(fp1, {**hit, 'file': 'src/other.js'}) is False
    # missing signature -> no match
    assert matches(fp1, {**hit, 'code': 'foo()'}) is False


def test_filter_findings_drops_fps_keeps_rest():
    pats = load_fp_patterns(DATA)
    findings = [
        {'cwe': 'CWE-346', 'file': 'src/sep24.js', 'code': 'postMessage(x)'},   # fp_001
        {'cwe': 'CWE-89', 'file': 'db.py', 'code': 'query(f"...")'},            # real
        {'cwe': 'CWE-95', 'file': 'a.py', 'code': 'ast.literal_eval(s)'},      # fp_006
    ]
    out = filter_findings(findings, pats)
    assert len(out) == 1
    assert out[0]['cwe'] == 'CWE-89'


def test_filter_findings_no_patterns_keeps_all():
    findings = [{'cwe': 'CWE-1', 'file': 'a', 'code': 'b'}]
    assert filter_findings(findings, []) == findings

```
